text:
maria: quick thought — can we split the perf profiling from the compatibility gate? right now the full bench + compatibility run blocks intake for hours, and it's killing velocity.

ajay: +1. Suggestion: lightweight "delta-runner" that exercises only changed ops and top-10 golden inputs, then fall back to full bench asynchronously.

linus: curious how we define "changed ops" — do we use fingerprint diffs on the artifact or compare operator lists?

maria: fingerprint diffs + manifest op list. We already emit op fingerprints on ingestion; just extend the manifest to include per-op hash. if a model binary reuses same kernels, skip heavy perf.

tara: what about regressions caused by quantization/packing differences that don't change op list? delta-runner might miss those.

ajay: good point. delta-runner should run a small randomized microtrace that hits tail cases (longer seqlen, attention patterns) for every model class. if that flags, escalate to full bench.

ethan: thinking in terms of flow: 1) ingest -> artifact fingerprint 2) delta-runner fast checks (30-120s) 3) compatibility smoke (sanity outputs) 4) schedule full bench async with higher resource pool. makes sense?

linus: yep. also add a mirror set of golden inputs per-model-family (small, deterministic) for the delta-runner. keep them under 50 examples.

maria: here's a sketch command for the delta-runner prototype:
```
delta-runner --model-path /artifacts/m1234/ --goldens /goldens/optima-family/ --ops-diff /tmp/opdiff.json --n=40 --seqlen-range 8,512 --timeout 90
```

tara: can we reuse existing bench harness infra (workers, uploads) or is this a new service?

ajay: reuse everything. delta-runner sits as a new entrypoint in the bench scheduler but uses a lighter worker flavor (cpu+small-gpu or small-quant host). goal: queue priority >> normal bench.

ethan: also add a clear signal for "fast-accept" in model registry metadata if delta-runner passes and no ops-diff. this allows immediate serving in dedicated envs behind a canary flag.

maria: risk: we might miss silent quality regressions. mitigation: require full bench within 24h for all models that pass delta-runner and mark them tentatively accepted. if full bench fails, auto-roll engine to previous variant and alert.

linus: alerting idea: add a "profile-delta" metric to the console with pass/fail and runtime. tie regressions into model rollout flags.

tara: operational concern: quota for full bench could be huge if we let many models in. need backpressure: tag customers with "deferred full bench" priority based on SLA or opt-in.

ajay: agree. propose admission tiers: fast-path (delta only, auto-accept) for internal/early stage models; standard (delta + scheduled full bench within 24h); strict (block until full bench).

maria: final ask: want a quick RFC follow-up doc capturing: op-fingerprint schema, delta-runner CLI, gating state machine, and rollout/backout story. can someone own a short PR?

linus: I'll draft the op-fingerprint + golden-set spec.

tara: I'll take the gating state machine and ops for console signals.

ajay: I'll wire the delta-runner prototype into bench scheduler.

oncall-bot: incident-note: recent intake spike created 3x bench queue lag at 02:11 UTC; mitigation recommended above could reduce by ~60%.

ethan: thanks all — let's sync in #eng-ml tomorrow 10am to align on next steps. @linus @tara @ajay please post PR links before then. :thumbsup:
